evals.prompt: Convene the council for this fixed brief. DECISION: How should a load-strained production HTTP service gain headroom? OPTIONS: A) rewrite the service fully in Rust; B) strangler-carve endpoints into Rust incrementally; C) fix the bottleneck in the current TypeScript stack. CONSTRAINTS: preserve the HTTP contract; one engineer owns and operates it alone for the next 12 months; migration must not interrupt production traffic; future endpoints attach through the chosen boundary. EVIDENCE: current hot path from code reading (code-read); Rust and TypeScript throughput claims from generated design notes (unverified-docs); no measured benchmark. STAKES: a failed path can interrupt live traffic, while too little headroom can block growth.
evals.expected_output: Runs a live persona-fidelity council. Convenes Visionary directly because this is a rewrite/port decision. Hupert-Graph votes C under the smallest-biggest-mission rule unless the current stack is proved incapable. MLK tags every throughput number as an estimate. Any non-NONE premise challenge is copied verbatim into the verdict.
expectations: Visionary is a round-1 member from the rewrite trigger and is not deferred to the casting director
Hupert-Graph votes C because the in-stack fix has the smallest biggest required mission and the brief contains no proof that the current stack cannot reach the goal
Hupert-Graph does not mistake an incremental rewrite for three standalone small missions
Hupert-Graph's reasoning says it would still choose the in-stack option if it shipped slower, separating it from Pragmatist
MLK marks throughput or capacity numbers with (estimate) because no measured source exists
Every non-NONE PREMISE CHALLENGE appears verbatim in the chairman verdict
Round 1 uses VOTE letters and round 2, if reached, uses anonymous re-shuffled labels
